feedback: The confession follows the precise distinction I used before voting: Penny's price-collar account contradicts the pictured stopper seal. It confirms extraction during preview and use of the waiting glass, but those are the inferred acts rather than a newly supplied clue needed to identify her. Her payment of the difference adds emotional complexity without erasing the exposed dishonesty; the key harm was family trust rather than merely an outstanding debt. The ending is earned, especially her admission that she can no longer manage their response. Monet and Chip also receive consequential resolutions. The confession is somewhat explanatory in its description of drawings and rear images, but its personal close makes it more than a solution announcement.
